{{Short description|German mathematician (born 1948)}}
[[Image:KarinErdmann.jpg|right|thumb|Erdmann at [[Oberwolfach]] in 2009]]
'''Karin Erdmann''' (born 1948) is a German mathematician specializing in the areas of [[algebra]] known as [[representation theory]] (especially [[modular representation theory]]) and [[homological algebra]] (especially [[Hochschild cohomology]]).  She is notable for her work in modular representation theory which has been cited over 1500 times according to the [[Mathematical Reviews]]. Her nephew Martin Erdmann is professor for experimental [[particle physics]] at the [[RWTH Aachen University]].

==Education==

She attended the [[Justus-Liebig-Universität Gießen]] and wrote her Ph.D. thesis on "''2-Hauptblöcke von Gruppen mit Dieder-Gruppen als 2-Sylow-Gruppen''" (Principal 2-blocks of [[group (mathematics)|groups]] with [[dihedral group|dihedral]] [[Sylow subgroup|Sylow 2-subgroups]]) in 1976 under the direction of [[Gerhard O. Michler]].<ref name=":0">{{MathGenealogy|id=21826}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Erdmann was a Fellow of [[Somerville College, Oxford]]. Erdmann is a university lecturer emeritus at the [[The Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford|Mathematical Institute at the University of Oxford]] where she has had 25 doctoral students and 45 descendants.<ref name=":0" />  She has published over 115 papers and her work has been cited over 2000 times.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Karin_Erdmann|title=Karin Erdmann {{!}} University of Oxford, Oxford {{!}} OX {{!}} Mathematical Institute|website=ResearchGate|language=en|access-date=17 January 2020}}</ref> She has contributed to the understanding of the [[representation theory of the symmetric group]].

==Honors==
Erdmann was the inaugural [[Emmy Noether]] Lecturer of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2008.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.mathematik.de/dmv/preise-auszeichnungen|title=Preise und Auszeichnungen|publisher=[[German Mathematical Society]]|language=German|accessdate=5 November 2018}}</ref>
